strengths: Addresses clear gap: First fact-checking benchmark with natural language explanations in non-English (Chinese) scenarios, combining real-world trending data with professional fact-checking sources
Rigorous dataset construction: Multi-stage pipeline with LLM voting, manual filtering, and quality assurance via 3+ independent reviewers per sample from prestigious institutions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests 6 diverse LLMs (reasoning-enhanced and general-purpose) plus existing methods, with ablation studies validating FactISR components
Practical relevance: Trending platform data avoids Wikipedia artifacts; diverse domains (health, politics, economics) reflect real-world use cases
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with informative figures, concrete examples, and transparent construction methodology
weaknesses: FactISR lacks methodological novelty: Primarily sophisticated prompt engineering combining existing concepts (CoT, iterative reasoning); Equation 1 underexplains iteration behavior and token triggering; no comparison to recent prompting strategies; missing sensitivity analysis on hyperparameters (Δ₀=20, γ=0.1)

ECS metric insufficiently validated: Manually categorized 5-level scale without learned components; no inter-annotator agreement for ECS itself; assumes categories correlate with explanation quality without evidence; evaluation via GPT-4o introduces potential bias

Missing human evaluation despite core claims: Paper emphasizes explanations for interpretability/trustworthiness yet provides NO human evaluation of explanation quality; relies entirely on surface metrics (BLEU-4 known poor for generation); cannot confirm explanations support fact-checking

Experimental rigor gaps: No statistical significance testing; crude label extraction via fuzzy matching with unquantified error propagation; zero inter-annotator agreement statistics for dataset annotations; absent error analysis and failure case studies

Dataset limitations: 7,643 samples modest vs. comparable benchmarks (FEVEROUS 87K); multi-evidence set only 1,131 (14.8%) severely imbalanced; trending data requires significant manual rewriting creating artificial claims; no human-performance baseline; temporal leakage risk (2020-2024 data vs. LLM training cutoffs unaddressed)

Weak analysis and unjustified claims: Minimal explanation for why inference-scaled models underperform on explanation generation; no domain-level difficulty analysis; 'evidence triangulation' term misleading for 2-component process; no ablation on template structure or parameter sensitivity

Reproducibility concerns: Dataset release not explicitly committed to; code availability unmentioned; some hyperparameter choices unjustified; inconsistent notation (7,643 vs 7,614 samples; ESC vs ECS)

strengths: Addresses real gap in non-English fact-checking benchmarks by creating the first Chinese dataset with structured natural language explanations
Rigorous multi-stage dataset construction with 4-reviewer quality validation and diverse sources (trending platforms + CHEF)
Comprehensive evaluation across 6+ state-of-the-art LLMs (o1-preview, DeepSeek-R1, QwQ, GPT-4) and existing fact-checking methods
Well-motivated problem: explanation generation is important but underexplored in fact-checking research
Demonstrates that leading reasoning models (o1-preview at 78.98%) still fall short of 80% accuracy, validating benchmark difficulty
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: FactISR is primarily prompt engineering (Evidence Triangulation is structured CoT) plus simple logit manipulation (reward decoding), without conceptual advancement
ECS metric poorly validated: no inter-rater agreement reported, evaluation procedure vague (does GPT-4o categorize?), creates circular dependency when evaluating explanations
ISR component provides only marginal gains (2.17 percentage points over ET alone), suggesting limited contribution of the proposed self-reflection mechanism
Experimental results underwhelming: FactISR (75.45%) does not exceed o1-preview baseline (78.98%), contradicting claims of 'outstanding improvements'
Contradictory results on explanation generation: inference-optimized models underperform on BLEU/ROUGE despite high ECS scores, suggests metric misalignment
Extreme dataset filtering (500K→7.6K, 1.5% retention) with no analysis of what was filtered or potential representativeness issues
Dataset size (7,643 samples) is smaller than many recent benchmarks (FlawCheck 30K+, QUANTEMP 30K+), limiting potential impact
Missing critical details: no inter-annotator agreement statistics, no error analysis by reasoning type, label extraction procedure vague (fuzzy matching to 3-way classification unclear)
No statistical significance testing of results; no confidence intervals or p-values reported
Reproducibility concerns: dataset availability unclear, hyperparameter choices (Δ₀=20, γ=0.1) unjustified, no sensitivity ablations

strengths: Addresses important gap in multilingual fact-checking: first Chinese benchmark with structured natural language explanations
Rigorous multi-stage dataset construction with quality review (4 annotators per sample) ensuring high-quality annotations
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple LLM categories (reasoning-enhanced and general-purpose) demonstrating benchmark difficulty (best model o1-preview achieves only 79% accuracy)
Practical relevance through diverse real-world sources (trending platforms + professional fact-checking repositories) rather than relying solely on Wikipedia
Thorough ablation studies showing both FactISR components (Evidence Triangulation and Iterative Self-Reflection) meaningfully improve baseline performance (10.14% accuracy gain)
Well-motivated identification of three key gaps in existing benchmarks: missing explanations, English-centric bias, temporal relevance
weaknesses: ECS metric lacks clear validation: methodology for assigning scores (1-5) is unclear, no inter-annotator agreement reported, no evidence that ECS correlates with actual factual correctness

FactISR method has limited novelty: evidence triangulation is essentially structured prompting for relevance/consistency/conflict checks; reward decoding via token manipulation (Eq. 1) appears ad-hoc with unjustified design choices (why γ^i decay?)
Reproducibility concerns: predefined token sequence S in reward decoding never specified; hyperparameters R=20, γ=0.1 lack justification or ablation; LLMs used for filtering/voting never identified
Missing data quality analysis: no inter-annotator agreement for final labels, no cross-source comparison, claim rewriting process could introduce biases with no documented analysis

Explanation evaluation problematic: relies on surface-level text metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE, BERTScore) that don't measure actual explanation quality; no human evaluation of whether explanations are helpful; finding that general-purpose models outperform reasoning models appears driven by text similarity rather than quality

Insufficient analysis of proposed methods: Table 2 ablation doesn't isolate ISR alone; no sensitivity analysis on reward hyperparameters; term 'evidence triangulation' is misleading (it's a verification template, not geometric triangulation)
Limited dataset characteristic analysis: no statistics on explanation length/complexity, temporal relevance claim not deeply validated, no detailed breakdown of data distribution across sources

Evaluation methodology issues: rule-based label extraction via FuzzyWuzzy is crude and unvalidated; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; inconsistent evaluation infrastructure (different models for different metrics)

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark addressing genuine gaps: emphasis on explanation generation, hotspot perception, and non-English language coverage fills real needs in fact-checking research
Rigorous data construction with comprehensive annotation pipeline (LLM + manual filtering, claim rewriting, evidence retrieval, explanation annotation) and evidence library of 66,217 entries
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple method types (traditional, LLMs, RLMs) revealing genuine difficulty of the benchmark (SOTA models achieve only ~72-74% verification accuracy)
Novel metrics (ECS and HCPI) operationalize previously unmeasured aspects—explanation consistency and hotspot-aware evaluation—addressing real evaluation gaps
Practical ablations and efficiency analysis demonstrate value of proposed components (e.g., DEA achieving ~50% reduction in reasoning time and input length)
weaknesses: Chinese-only language severely limits impact, reproducibility, and adoption in the international NLP community; no discussion of transferability to other languages

Explanation generation quality is alarmingly low (BLEU-4 scores 0.21-0.30); critical disparity between RLM verification performance and explanation quality inadequately analyzed, suggesting unresolved fundamental challenges

FactISR method is incremental (1-2% accuracy improvements) and tightly coupled to specific RLM architectures with reward decoding; limited generalizability and lack of theoretical justification for design choices (Eq. 1 parameters appear ad-hoc)

Evidence retrieval is an underexamined bottleneck: R@5 of 78.97% and 5-10% performance jumps with gold evidence suggest artificially difficult evidence library; evidence construction via LLM-based paraphrasing may not reflect realistic fact-checking scenarios

HCPI metric combines multiple components with apparently arbitrary weights (α=0.05, β=0.2, κ=0.15, λ=0.6) without ablation or sensitivity analysis; no validation that metric correlates with real-world hotspot perception capability
Data augmentation transparency issues: inter-annotator agreement not reported, annotation costs/time not disclosed, LLM-based claim rewriting may introduce systematic biases
Limited analysis and insights: no domain-level performance breakdown, error analysis, qualitative failure cases, or investigation into what makes hotspot perception or multi-hop reasoning difficult

Dataset composition undermines stated focus: 85% single-evidence samples underexplore reasoning; only ~15% retain hotspot indicators, limiting the benchmark's ability to evaluate its primary stated goal

Technical concerns: no statistical significance testing, circular evaluation (ECS depends on GPT-4o), lack of inter-annotator agreement metrics, and gold evidence results highlight that evidence retrieval—not reasoning—is the primary bottleneck

strengths: Addresses documented gaps with Chinese-language fact-checking benchmark including natural language explanations
Reasonably large dataset (7,643 samples) with substantial evidence library (66,217 entries) and careful multi-stage annotation procedures
Comprehensive experimental evaluation covering multiple model types (traditional, LLMs, RLMs) with ablation studies
Practical focus on trending/hotspot events grounds benchmark in real-world misinformation scenarios
Inclusion of influence/hotspot metadata provides rich sample attributes
weaknesses: Core 'hotspot perception' concept lacks rigorous definition; connection between trending metadata and fact-checking performance is asserted but never validated
HCPI metric is complex but poorly justified—arbitrary weight choices (α=0.05, β=0.2, κ=0.15, λ=0.6), asymmetric label treatment, and no validation against human judgment or external criteria

FactISR method is incremental (conditional evidence selection + structured prompting + token probability adjustment) with only 1-2% accuracy improvements and unclear generalization beyond this dataset
Evidence retrieval bottleneck (R@5=78.97% best case) but gold evidence enables 77-79% accuracy, suggesting difficulty is retrieval-based rather than conceptual reasoning
Critical analysis gaps: no error analysis, no case studies, no investigation of which reasoning types or domains are hardest, no human evaluation of explanation quality beyond automated metrics
Inter-annotator agreement for annotations not reported; claim rewriting process (six factors) appears ad-hoc without principled justification or bias analysis
No evidence that considering hotspot indicators improves fact-checking performance; design choice appears engineered for this specific benchmark rather than grounded in theory

Reproducibility concerns: no statement on dataset release, no inter-annotator agreement metrics, implementation details scattered across appendices, potential data contamination risk (2020-2024 events may be in LLM training data)
Paper attempts to bundle three loosely-connected contributions (benchmark + metrics + method) at reduced depth; contribution boundaries are unclear and would benefit from more focused scope

strengths: Novel benchmark addressing real gaps: First hotspot perception fact-checking benchmark in Chinese scenario with comprehensive three-task evaluation (verification, retrieval, explanation). Practical focus on emerging trending events fills a clear need.

Rigorous benchmark construction: Multi-stage annotation process with manual claim rewriting following 6 systematic factors, quality control reviews, and evidence library construction shows substantial effort and methodological care.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests diverse model types (RLMs, LLMs, traditional methods), multiple retrieval approaches, and includes ablation studies demonstrating each FactISR component contributes meaningfully.

Appropriately challenging dataset: Even state-of-the-art models (QwQ-32B: 72.67% accuracy) fall well below acceptable performance, indicating the benchmark captures real difficulty. Provides meaningful benchmark for future research.

Well-motivated methodology: FactISR's three components are grounded in observations about RLM behavior and human reasoning patterns. The DEA efficiency gains (50% reduction in reasoning time/input length) are notable.
Comprehensive metrics framework: Moving beyond standard BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore, ECS captures explanation-verification alignment and HCPI integrates multiple dimensions of hotspot perception capability.
Strong practical relevance: Uses real trending platform data (more timely than Wikipedia), addresses challenge of emerging misinformation, and acknowledges real-world deployment considerations.
weaknesses: Missing critical annotation analysis: No inter-annotator agreement (IAA) scores reported—essential for validating dataset quality. No details on annotation training procedure, kappa scores, or disagreement resolution strategy provided.

Inadequate justification for design choices: HCPI's weight parameters (α=0.05, β=0.2, κ=0.15, λ=0.6) and ECS's 5-level categorization lack principled justification. No sensitivity analysis shows robustness to these hyperparameters. The GPT-4o computed 'influence score' methodology is unexplained.

Hotspot indicator metrics not validated: The four indicators (views, discussions, posts, engagements) appear platform-specific without theoretical grounding. Why are these the right metrics for measuring genuine societal impact vs. algorithmic amplification? No human evaluation validates this framing.

FactISR method lacks clarity and generality: DEA's 'specific signals' for evidence injection are vaguely described. Why is the 'yes' token appropriate for the reward mechanism? Method shows only modest improvements (1.65-2.37%) and appears heavily engineered for specific models. Limited generalization evidence.

Evidence library construction methodology problematic: Using LLM-generated paraphrases (relevance >0.6) introduces systematic bias. No human evaluation of paraphrase quality or diversity. Distribution of 66,217 evidence items across domains not reported. Circular use of LLM may create spurious task artifacts.

Severe limitation in scope: Chinese-language-only benchmark significantly reduces international applicability and impact. No discussion of cross-lingual transferability or path to multilingual extension. Limits generalizability of findings.

Missing essential error and ablation analyses: No error analysis by claim type or domain. No analysis of FactISR performance across hotspot levels. No case studies showing when/why method helps or fails. Qualitative explanation analysis absent. Gold evidence experiments (Appendix I) show evidence retrieval is major bottleneck—not adequately discussed.

Reproducibility concerns: Critical FactISR prompt details 'omitted for space constraints.' No code/data release plan mentioned. Many hyperparameters (R=20, γ=0.1) lack principled justification. Dataset construction heavily manual (15 annotators)—scaling and reproducibility across new annotators unclear.

Novel metrics not validated against human judgment: ECS and HCPI are proposed without comparison to human evaluations of explanation quality. No demonstration that these metrics correlate with human preferences. Validation against alternative explanation metrics missing.

Inconsistent benchmark design: ~15% of samples have null hotspot indicators to 'assess fundamental verification abilities,' creating an inconsistent evaluation protocol. This design choice suggests hotspot perception evaluation wasn't fully integrated.
